text:
oncall-bot: INCIDENT ALERT - High CPU on preproc pods in us-west-2 (service: prompt-preprocessor). Multiple pods reporting OOMKilled and container restarts. Pager: #incidents. https://monitoring/redwood/alerts/2345

elaine: ack. pinging oncall. do we have a customer impact estimate yet? :eyes:

tariq: I'm oncall, taking this. starting live debug. first glance: several preproc replicas maxing 100% CPU and then OOM/killed.

samira: CS: we're getting alerts from two customers (acme-inc, studyapp) about 5xx and cut streams. they reported a spike starting ~2m ago.

tariq: copying relevant logs from one pod:

```
Jan 09 12:03:21 preproc-72f4 kubelet[...]: Container preproc terminated with OOMKilled
2026-01-09T12:03:20Z ERROR tokenizer: recursive token expansion exceeded memory budget
stack: tokenize->normalize->vocab_lookup
```

and top output shows consistent 98-100% CPU in the process `redwood-preproc` across threads.

kyle: possible thesis: a bad prompt or customer pattern caused the preproc hotpath to spin (regex/backtracking or expansion). Can we throttle ingress or add short-lived concurrency cap? Quick mitigation: add `X-Client-Rate-Limit` drop for heavy keys or route that traffic to a lower-priority queue.

tariq: putting a temporary 50% rate limit on the routing rule for streaming endpoint for non-enterprise customers now.

```
# routerctl apply
routerctl set-rate-limit --route "/v1/stream" --match "!tier:enterprise" --qps 10
```

infra-bot: HPA events: scaled preproc-deployment from 6 -> 10 replicas due to sustained CPU > 85% over 2m. Node k8s-node-7 showing kubelet eviction warnings.

elaine: ok scale helpful but nodes are filling. if nodes have swap pressure we could see more OOMs. consider cordon/drain the worst node.

tariq: identifying worst node with most evictions: k8s-node-7 (us-west-2a). cordoning and draining now.

```
kubectl cordon k8s-node-7
kubectl drain k8s-node-7 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --grace-period=30
```

kube: drain started, several pods evicted, one preproc pod restarted successfully on k8s-node-3.

samira: CS update: acme-inc still seeing partial failures (~20% of requests). informing customers that we're mitigating and will follow up.

kyle: long-term quick fix: add concurrency limit in tokenizer config to avoid unbounded regex backtracking and make tokenization OOM-resistant. Pushing a hotfix config to `preproc-config` to cap `max_token_expansion=5000` and `concurrency=8`.

```
# configmap patch
kubectl patch configmap preproc-config -n platform --type merge -p '{"data":{"tokenizer.max_token_expansion":"5000","tokenizer.concurrency":"8"}}'
```

tariq: applied patch, triggering rolling restart of preproc deployment.

```
kubectl rollout restart deployment/preproc -n platform
```

oncall-bot: Observability: 5xx rate for /v1/stream peaked at 12% -> trending down to 3% after rate-limit and restart. CPU utilization across preproc pool down to 45% median.

kyle: added a short circuit in preproc to detect pathological inputs and fail fast with 429 instead of spinning — will open PR for full fix.

tariq: handing off to kyle for the next 60m (he's nearest to the PRs and infra changes). Summary for handoff:
- root cause: prompt/preproc hotpath (regex/token expansion) -> CPU spin -> OOMKilled
- mitigations performed: temporary router rate-limit, scaled replicas, cordoned/drained k8s-node-7, patched configmap to cap expansion/concurrency, rollout restart of preproc
- customer impact: acme-inc & studyapp saw 5xx and partial stream failures; mitigated, CS notified
- followups: kyle to land tokenizer fail-fast and more robust limits; infra to check node provisioning and eviction thresholds; obs to add anomaly alert for token expansion growth

elaine: thanks. i'll update the incident log + CS message thread. handing off fully to kyle. :white_check_mark:

kyle: taking over. will monitor for 1h then close if stable. tagging followups in JIRA: RED-3241 (tokenizer fail-fast), RED-3242 (node eviction tuning).

cs-bot: Noted customer notify: acme-inc updated; next update in 30m.

oncall-bot: Incident state -> mitigated. open actions remain. oncall owner: kyle.
